th 02/Dated: 20 July, 2023 I.A. No.5279 of 2023:
1.

This interlocutory application has been filed for condoning the delay of 144 days,
which has occurred in preferring this appeal.
2. No counter affidavit to the delay condonation application has been filed.

3. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
4. Having heard the learned counsel for the appellants and considering the statements made in this application, we are of the view that the appellants were prevented by sufficient cause in preferring this appeal within time.
5.
Accordingly, this interlocutory application is allowed and the delay of 144 days in preferring this appeal, is hereby condoned.

sentences.text: 6. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.

7. Admit.
8.
Mr. Vineet Kr. Vashistha, learned APP waives notice on behalf of the respondent-State.

9. Call for the LCR from the court concerned.
10.
Office is directed to prepare the paper-book and supply to the concerned parties.

11. The instant application has been filed under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C. seeking therein suspension of sentence in connection with the judgment of conviction dated 22.11.2022 and order of sentence dated 23.11.2022 passed by the learned Special Judge (POCSO Act), Dhanbad in Spl. (POCSO) Case No. 80 of 2019 arising out of Pathrdih P.S. Case No. 17 of 2019, by which the appellant has been convicted and sentenced to undergo imprisonment for life for the offence under Section 376 (AB) of IPC alongwith fine of Rs.5,000/- and in default of payment of fine, has been further directed to undergo additional imprisonment for one month.
12.

Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that the prosecution has miserably failed in proving the charge beyond all shadow of doubt if the testimony of P.W.- 1 will be taken into consideration with the testimony of P.W.- 3, the father of the victim.
It has been contended that the P.W.- 1 in her cross-examination has deposed
that she has made statement in course of her examination as was asked by her father to say.

13. Learned counsel for the appellant, therefore, has submitted that the testimony of P.W.-1 is not reliable since whatever statement has been made by her, that is being tutored by her father but the learned trial court has given reliance upon the same while convicting the appellant.

It has further been contended that even the doctor has not corroborated the commission of crime as would appear from the suggestion given by him wherein it has been deposed by the doctor that hymen can also be torn by cycling.
Learned counsel for the appellant, on the basis of the aforesaid premise, has submitted that it is a fit case where the sentence may be suspended.

14. While on the other hand, Mr. Vineet Kr. Vashistha, learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondent-State of Jharkhand has submitted that the testimony of P.W.-1 cannot be discarded if it will be considered in entirety since she has fully supported the prosecution version Rajan Manjhi vs The State Of Jharkhand on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107059142/
2 by supporting the fact of commission of crime by the appellant.

sentences.text: It has been submitted that so far as the contention that the victim has stated in the cross-examination that she has deposed whatever has been asked to say by her father, on the basis of the same, the entire prosecution of the P.W.- 1 cannot be discarded.
Moreover, the doctor has fully supported the prosecution version since the doctor has found that hymen was torn and the victim was aged about 08 years and when the hymen was torn.
Learned APP on the aforesaid premise, has submitted that the instant application may be rejected.

15. This Court has heard the learned counsel for the parties, perused the finding recorded by the learned trial court in the impugned judgment wherefrom it is evident from the bare perusal of the testimony of P.W.- 1, the victim who happens to be of 08 years, that she has fully supported the prosecution version.

P.W.- 2 has also fully supported the same as would appear from the testimony of P.W.- 2 wherein it has been deposed by her, as has been taken note by the learned trial court at paragraph-15 of the impugned judgment, that when she returned to her house at about 06:00 in the evening her daughter, the victim, told that the appellant, namely, Rajan Manjhi, has opened her pant and committed dirty work and when she saw her private parts by removing her pants, P.W.- 2 noticed that there was bleeding from her way of urination and there was redness in that body part.
Thereafter, she went to the police station for registering the complaint.
P.W.- 8, the doctor, has also supported the prosecution version.
It has been deposed by the P.W.- 8 that the radiological age of the victim was less than 08 years and the hymen was torn.
16. This Court, on the basis of the fact that the ocular evidence is being corroborated by the medical evidence, is of the view that that it is not a fit case where the sentence is to be suspended.
17. Accordingly, the instant interlocutory application stands rejected.
18. However, any observation made hereinabove, will not prejudice the merit of the case since the criminal case is lying pending.

(Sujit Narayan Prasad, J.) (Subhash Chand, J.) Saurabh/-
